Why: Connects planning with emotional capacity and answers whether the student can carry more.
What we learned: The strongest idea was a capacity-aware planning tool, not another generic to-do list.
Evidence in final app: Dashboard, task load calculation, What-if, Balance, Care, Journal.

Why: Mentor feedback asked how workload is calculated, so the score needed a visible source.
What we learned: A credible workload score needs task inputs.
Evidence in final app: Task form collects time, category, start date, due date, flexibility, and reminder.

Why: Conflicting numbers across pages would break trust.
What we learned: Consistency is a product decision, not only a technical decision.
Evidence in final app: Dashboard, Tasks, What-if, and Balance use shared workload logic.

Why: Students accept extra work before seeing the cost.
What we learned: Prevention is more novel than only recovery.
Evidence in final app: What-if previews projected load before accepting a commitment.

Why: Overload needs concrete action, not just advice.
What we learned: Balance should reduce overload without forcing deletion.
Evidence in final app: User chooses move, keep, or drop, with AI plan confirmation.

Why: Helpful only if it suggests enough change, not too much.
What we learned: Automation must stay user-controlled.
Evidence in final app: Auto plan modal requires confirm and can be adjusted.

Why: Users may dislike the app's suggested schedule.
What we learned: Suggested plans should stay editable.
Evidence in final app: Edit controls update title, category, hours, dates, reminder, priority, and flexibility.

Why: A plan is more useful if the app nudges before work starts.
What we learned: Small reminder settings make the prototype feel complete.
Evidence in final app: Users can choose no reminder, 5 min, 10 min, or 30 min before.

Why: Students need to see what is active on one selected day.
What we learned: Date-range tasks must appear on every active day.
Evidence in final app: Multi-day tasks show across start-to-due range.

Why: Burnout is clearer at week level.
What we learned: Balance should work at weekly level.
Evidence in final app: Weekly plan shows selected week, daily loads, and active tasks.

Why: Stress is emotional as well as logistical.
What we learned: Journal can turn feelings into wellbeing insight.
Evidence in final app: User records mood and notes; Lumi can analyze pressure and suggest comfort.

Why: Students overload because saying no is hard.
What we learned: Boundary setting is part of workload management.
Evidence in final app: User describes a situation and gets soft, firm, or short replies.

Why: Users need immediate small resets when stressed.
What we learned: Recovery should be tiny and actionable.
Evidence in final app: Breath, wooden fish tapping, and bubble popping.

Why: Users may not know the real pressure source.
What we learned: Identify the pressure before choosing the solution.
Evidence in final app: Reflect asks one small question based on guilt, deadline, people pressure, or messy stress.

Why: Too much community made the app crowded and less focused.
What we learned: Workload clarity should come first.
Evidence in final app: Community remains secondary.

Why: Games alone do not solve planning or overload.
What we learned: Mini games should support recovery, not define the product.
Evidence in final app: Mini games sit under Care.

Why: Too generic and does not show capacity.
What we learned: A list alone cannot prevent burnout.
Evidence in final app: Tasks are inputs for load calculation.

Why: Time blocks do not capture mental, social, or physical load.
What we learned: Time and workload are related but not identical.
Evidence in final app: Load uses effort weight and task dimensions.

Why: Comfort without task action feels generic.
What we learned: Emotional support should connect to planning action.
Evidence in final app: Lumi supports planning, Boundary, Reflect, and Journal.

Why: Users disliked the app deciding for them.
What we learned: The app should suggest, not control.
Evidence in final app: User confirms before AI changes apply.

Why: Moving work within the same week may not reduce weekly pressure.
What we learned: Balance should move tasks out of the overloaded week when needed.
Evidence in final app: Move sends flexible tasks to next week.
